ranking.note: Raised to P1: it is the category-defining decoupling work (removes cs_main from index sync), fixes startup/reindex race conditions and stale reorg data, and unblocks out-of-process indexing (#10102), wallet rescan reuse (#15719) and the ownership cleanup in #35474.
Placed ahead of the larger parallelization win because #26966 builds on this batching foundation; reviewing it first unblocks the chain.
Kept P3: the data-integrity gain is real but most of the patch lands in coins/dbwrapper (validation); its index-facing effect overlaps with #35728.

inconsistencies: #35728 and #34132 both address the same defect class: index/database read corruption being reported as a missing record. #35728 is the narrow, index-scoped fix and should be reviewed first; #34132 generalizes the policy at the dbwrapper layer and may subsume it, so a decision on which layer owns the behaviour is needed before both land.
Chain: #34489 (batched index writes) is stated groundwork for #26966 (parallel index sync); review #34489 first or the parallelization will be rebased twice.

#24230 and #35474 both restructure how indexes are owned and reach node state (interfaces vs NodeContext). #24230 is the broader framework change and should set the direction; #35474 should be reviewed against it rather than independently.

#35229 converts CChain/CBlockIndex pointers to references in the very index and chain APIs that #24230 removes from the index layer entirely; it is low priority and should not be allowed to churn ahead of #24230.
result.notes: The list splits cleanly: one framework/correctness project (#24230) at P1, three substantive user-visible items (feature + two sync speedups) at P2, four smaller correctness/housekeeping items at P3, and one pure janitorial refactor at P4. No compression was needed.
